Fake Alcohol

By: Sibusisiwe Buthelezi | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We take a look at the trade of counterfeit alcohol, how it's made, sold and how it affects you at home.

Unique Selling Point:
We have an insider sharing how the fake alcohol is made. Secondly, we confront a brewer where manufacturers of illicit alcohol are purchasing the ingredients.

Lastly, we will approach the story from the perspective of the middle class but also explore how it is affecting those of a lower income class, essentially emphasising the point that fake alcohol is a national crisis.

Summary:
Over the last two years, South Africa has seen a spike in counterfeit alcohol making its way to communities across the
country. At first it seemed like small scale “backdoor” brewers who were creating cheaper versions of spirits but that’s not the case.

We have uncovered a legitimate brewery in Boksburg that supplies ingredients to alcohol manufacturers, who then
brew and sell counterfeit alcohol on the black market. They recycle packaging of Remy Martin, Hennesy, Jack Daniels and different variations of gin.

The long and short of it is that the boom of fake alcohol is a national crisis that is affected all South Africans, regardless of race or class.

Press Release:


Mocktails Uncapped

From cigarettes to sneakers, sanitary pads to sweaters… anything can be counterfeited. But have you ever suspected your favourite
bottle of spirits might not be what it appears? Counterfeit alcohol sales are spiking across the country – and it’s not only the work of small-scale “backdoor” brewers. In Boksburg, an apparently legitimate brewer supplies ingredients to black-market manufacturers.
An insider tells us how it’s done, from manufacturing to packaging it in recycled bottles for sale… not only on the black market, but in mainstream shops and restaurants. Meanwhile, consumers pay the price – in some cases, with their lives. Carte Blanche gets
a taste of the trade.

Producer: Sebe Buthelezi | Presenter: Govan Whittles

Script:


(Govan) Ranked the 5 th biggest alcohol consumer on the globe-
(Govan) It’s clear many South Africans love their liquor.
(Neo Malatji) It’s just a matter of coming home sometimes, getting a glass, being
relaxed.
(Govan) But where there’s a demand, almost inevitably a black market emerges – in this
case one with dangerous consequences.
(Govan) How do you make sure that people can’t tell that it’s fake?
(Hidden) Because gin tastes like gin.
(Govan) Counterfeit gin, laced with methanol.
(Shamal Ramesar) Methanol is associated with irreversible blindness…and in most
cases results in death.
(Govan) It’s an illicit market fed by large scale suppliers and backroom dealers… one
we were compelled to investigate.
(Govan) Why are you selling ingredients to make fake alcohol?
(Leon Strydom) Everyone, I think, is, I suppose is trying to make a living.
(Counterfeit video) This is our business as you can see..
(Govan) Videos like these showing the manufacture of counterfeit alcohol are all over
social media.
(Counterfeit video) Yoh, yoh, yoh. Are you trying to kill us. You’ll think you are buying
Hennesy. But you are buying stuff made by this guy…
(Govan) Have you ever had a hangover that just won’t go away, days after a night out.
Or a suppressed appetite after getting a few drinks? If you have, then you may have
been drinking, fake alcohol.
(Govan) Joburg resident, Neo Malatji, suspects he consumed counterfeit alcohol in
December last year.
(Neo Malatji) My wife was not here, I had all the freedom.
(Govan) And he celebrated that freedom with his favorite cognac, Hennesy.
(Neo Malatji) On Sunday I woke up at around 3…I wasn’t feeling good at all. I was like
nah, it’s just a hangover.
(Neo Malatji) Monday it was even worse.

(Govan) What were the symptoms? How were you feeling?
(Neo Malatji) I was hot but I was feeling cold. I was wearing blankets.
(Govan) Did you have any pain?
(Neo Malatji) My stomach was in pain. That was horrible, that was the worst.
(Govan) Three days into his hangover, Neo called a friend who rushed him to hospital.
(Neo Malatji) I was actually screaming in the hospital, I was like yooh, guys I’m dying
here. So apparently my stomach lining was being eaten up by that fake alcohol.
(Govan) Did you think at that time that you had fake alcohol?
(Neo Malatji) At the time I’m thinking a lot of things right, until obviously it was confirmed
by my nurse that this is caused by fake alcohol.
(Govan) Head of research at Drinks Federation SA, Dr Shamal Ramesar, says
counterfeit alcohol is at crisis levels.
(Shamal Ramesar) We’re looking at a R 25 billion industry here.
(Govan) Dr Shamal says Neo is lucky to be alive after drinking counterfeit alcohol.
(Shamal Ramesar) We found some really toxic chemicals in that. For example the most
common chemical was methanol. The second one we found was industrial grade
ethanol.
(Govan) Both have potentially lethal side effects.
(Shamal Ramesar) Metabolic disorders such as acidosis, which leads to cardiac failure,
respiratory failure.
(Govan) Neo insists he bought his alcohol from a reputable outlet.
(Shamal Ramesar) Your known legitimate retail outlets are stocking illicit alcohol as well.
(Govan) Has illicit alcohol penetrated the formal market to an extent where they may not
know?
(Shamal Ramesar) The operations have become so sophisticated that it even finds
penetration in your formal sectors.
(Govan) This man began making counterfeit alcohol during the Covid pandemic.
(Govan) He agreed to talk to us if we hid his identity.
(Hidden) The demand for alcohol was so high then, that’s where I saw an opportunity
and I met a guy, who knows a guy who can get us that alcohol.

(Hidden) Then we started manufacturing it from the backyard of his house.
(Govan) What kind of brands do you target the most?
(Hidden) Most people like Belgravia, Gordons, Old Buck, We target the one that’s
rocking on the market.
(Shamal Ramesar) 53% of illicit alcohol by volume is made up of the spirit sector or
spirit category.
(Shamal Ramesar) They’ve become so good at mimicking and counterfeiting, even
industrial forensic experts are finding it difficult to now on face value or on sight, identify
the counterfeit products.
(Hidden) Everyone wants to drink in South Africa so why not?
(Govan) Do you ever feel bad about people getting sick?
(Hidden) No I don’t because we all die at the end my man and I’m giving them what they
want because if I don’t give them, someone else will. So why not?
(Govan) In Tembisa, east of Johannesburg, a different kind of Amapiano is making the
rounds.
(Bongani Liphondo) This thing is a problem, if you drink this thing you sleep the whole
day, you can’t eat..
(Bongani Liphondo) You lose appetite, you lose power. No drinking water.
(Govan) Bongani Liphondo is recovering from an addiction to amapiano: cheap, often
unbranded vodka, sold in sachets and tiny plastic bottles.
(Bongani Liphondo) If you drink this thing you get drunk quick.
(Govan) How much is it?
(Bongani Liphondo) R3, R5, R25, it’s different prices.
(Bongani Liphondo) You sleep, you wake up, still you are drunk. It’s got too much power
this thing.
(Shamal Ramesar) One in three people that we interviewed said that they know of
somebody who has physically died from consuming counterfeit alcohol.
(Govan) Bongani claims to have lost a friend to amapiano two months ago.
(Bongani Liphondo) He collapsed at the gate at the clinic.

(Govan) Can you imagine trying to establish what’s real and what’s fake among all of
this alcohol. It’s nearly impossible. And that’s the point, that one in every five bottles of
alcohol is probably fake. And chances are, you wouldn’t know which.
(Shamal Ramesar) If the seal doesn’t make a cracking sound when it’s opened, it
means that that bottle has been tampered with.
(Shamal Ramesar) Raise that bottle up and shake it and look at it through light. If there
are any particles that are floating in that bottle, it means that it’s been adulterated or
tampered with because distilled alcohol shouldn’t have any particles floating inside it.
(Govan) The alarming context sketched by Dr Ramesar coupled with the information
provided by the insider demanded further investigation. We went undercover to find out
where illicit alcohol manufacturers were getting their ingredients from.
(Govan) Our search led us to Beer Craft SA, where we met Leon Strydom.
(Leon Strydom) So what a lot of guys do is they, they get the alcohol and they buy the
flavoring from me. So you can make Hennessy. You can make Irish whiskey, which is
Jameson, scotch whiskey.
(Leon Strydom) Vodka, so you can make all those things yourself.
(Govan) Selling alcohol flavoring isn’t a crime, under the Liquor Products Act, but the
legality depends on what its intended for.
(Govan) It was clear Leon was fully aware that his products were being used to
manufacture illicit alcohol.
(CB Producer) In a box of Hennessy, there are 12 bottles-
(Leon Strydom) Yes.
(CB Producer) So for me to get that taste, how many of these do I use?
(Leon Strydom) So you are gonna make one batch with all the alcohol and all the water,
mix all of them and then just divide it up into 750, easiest.
(Leon Strydom) I'll give you a website where you can go for all the blending and
whatever. So it's quite easy.
(Govan) Our undercover footage in hand, we returned to Beer Craft SA.
(Govan) This time not as potential buyers but to hold Leon to account.
(Govan) So we’ve come to the east rand to go confront Leon Strydom. He’s the guy
that’s selling the ingredients to make fake alcohol.

(Govan) I wanna hear what he has to say for himself. How can he justify doing
something that gets people killed.
(Govan) Hey Leon, my name is Govan, I’m from Carte Blanche.
(Leon Strydom) Yes.
(Govan) I’d like to talk to you about your business please.
(Leon Strydom) Of course, yeah.
(Govan) We understand that you’re supplying the fake alcohol market.
(Leon Strydom) No.
(Govan) You sell ingredients to make fake alcohol.
(Leon Strydom) I’m selling flavoring.
(Govan) No, you sell ingredients to make fake alcohol. Do you know that what you’re
doing is illegal?
(Leon Strydom) Ok.
(Govan) Why are you selling ingredients to make fake alcohol?
(Leon Strydom) Everyone, I think, is, I suppose is trying to make a living. A lot of guys in
the area do that.
(Govan) We’ve been monitoring you for months. We know that you sell the ingredients
to sell fake Hennesy, you specify how to do it as well.
(Leon Strydom) I don’t specify how to do it.
(Govan) You give the people everything they need to make fake alcohol. Do you care
that people are dying from fake alcohol? From the stuff that you sell, the ingredients?
(Leon Strydom) Well I suppose it is quite- Obviously it’s… it’s not my intention to sell
anything that‘s gonna kill people but yah… I don’t know where they get their alcohol
from.
(Govan) We ask him about the counterfeit Hennesy.
(Leon Strydom) So it’s not really Hennesy. I can’t sell something that’s… what it says, it
says flavoring. I’ll have a vodka flavoring, I’ll have a brandy flavoring
(Govan) Of the big brands?
(Leon Strydom) No, not of the big brands at all.
(Govan) Isn’t Hennesy the big brand?

(Leon Strydom) It’s just my own stupid label that I’ve put on there
(Shamal Ramesar) These products are branded, they have specific formulations that IP
belongs to the manufacturer itself, so anybody that is trying to pass it off as a brand is
definitely in contravention of the laws.
(Govan) We suspect that you are actually supplying a large number of the
manufacturers in Johannesburg that make fake alcohol. They get their flavoring from
you.
(Leon Strydom) I’m just a small housebound business so I buy 5 litres of flavoring from
a guy, I put it into smaller bottles, I sell it. It’s not like a multimillion dollar or multi-million-
rand business that I’ve got.
(Govan) Right now you sell to anyone right? Doesn’t matter if you know what they are
doing or not?
(Leon Strydom) Well I don’t know what they are doing.
(Govan) So you sell to anyone?
(Leon Strydom) Yeah.
(Govan) In a written response, the police said vetting the authenticity of alcohol isn’t
their job but that of SARS.
(Govan) That’ll come as little consolation to people like Neo.
(Neo Malatji) You need to stop it with this fake alcohol because its killing us.
(Shamal Ramesar) We should look at investigating whether these products are causing
grievous bodily harm and even look at attempted murder charges.

(Hidden) No I don’t because we all die at the end my man and I’m giving them what they want because if I don’t give them, someone else will. So why not? (Govan) In Tembisa, east of Johannesburg, a different kind of Amapiano is making the rounds. (Bongani Liphondo) This thing is a problem, if you drink this thing you sleep the whole day, you can’t eat.. (Bongani Liphondo) You lose appetite, you lose power. No drinking water. (Govan) Bongani Liphondo is recovering from an addiction to amapiano: cheap, often unbranded vodka, sold in sachets and tiny plastic bottles. (Bongani Liphondo) If you drink this thing you get drunk quick. (Govan) How much is it? (Bongani Liphondo) R3, R5, R25, it’s different prices. (Bongani Liphondo) You sleep, you wake up, still you are drunk. It’s got too much power this thing. (Shamal Ramesar) One in three people that we interviewed said that they know of somebody who has physically died from consuming counterfeit alcohol. (Govan) Bongani claims to have lost a friend to amapiano two months ago. (Bongani Liphondo) He collapsed at the gate at the clinic. (Govan) Can you imagine trying to establish what’s real and what’s fake among all of this alcohol. It’s nearly impossible. And that’s the point, that one in every five bottles of alcohol is probably fake. And chances are, you wouldn’t know which. (Shamal Ramesar) If the seal doesn’t make a cracking sound when it’s opened, it means that that bottle has been tampered with. (Shamal Ramesar) Raise that bottle up and shake it and look at it through light. If there are any particles that are floating in that bottle, it means that it’s been adulterated or tampered with because distilled alcohol shouldn’t have any particles floating inside it. (Govan) The alarming context sketched by Dr Ramesar coupled with the information provided by the insider demanded further investigation. We went undercover to find out where illicit alcohol manufacturers were getting their ingredients from. (Govan) Our search led us to Beer Craft SA, where we met Leon Strydom. (Leon Strydom) So what a lot of guys do is they, they get the alcohol and they buy the flavoring from me. So you can make Hennessy. You can make Irish whiskey, which is Jameson, scotch whiskey. (Leon Strydom) Vodka, so you can make all those things yourself. (Govan) Selling alcohol flavoring isn’t a crime, under the Liquor Products Act, but the legality depends on what its intended for. (Govan) It was clear Leon was fully aware that his products were being used to manufacture illicit alcohol. (CB Producer) In a box of Hennessy, there are 12 bottles- (Leon Strydom) Yes. (CB Producer) So for me to get that taste, how many of these do I use? (Leon Strydom) So you are gonna make one batch with all the alcohol and all the water, mix all of them and then just divide it up into 750, easiest. (Leon Strydom) I'll give you a website where you can go for all the blending and whatever. So it's quite easy. (Govan) Our undercover footage in hand, we returned to Beer Craft SA. (Govan) This time not as potential buyers but to hold Leon to account. (Govan) So we’ve come to the east rand to go confront Leon Strydom. He’s the guy that’s selling the ingredients to make fake alcohol. (Govan) I wanna hear what he has to say for himself. How can he justify doing something that gets people killed. (Govan) Hey Leon, my name is Govan, I’m from Carte Blanche. (Leon Strydom) Yes. (Govan) I’d like to talk to you about your business please. (Leon Strydom) Of course, yeah. (Govan) We understand that you’re supplying the fake alcohol market. (Leon Strydom) No. (Govan) You sell ingredients to make fake alcohol. (Leon Strydom) I’m selling flavoring. (Govan) No, you sell ingredients to make fake alcohol. Do you know that what you’re doing is illegal? (Leon Strydom) Ok. (Govan) Why are you selling ingredients to make fake alcohol? (Leon Strydom) Everyone, I think, is, I suppose is trying to make a living. A lot of guys in the area do that. (Govan) We’ve been monitoring you for months. We know that you sell the ingredients to sell fake Hennesy, you specify how to do it as well. (Leon Strydom) I don’t specify how to do it. (Govan) You give the people everything they need to make fake alcohol. Do you care that people are dying from fake alcohol? From the stuff that you sell, the ingredients? (Leon Strydom) Well I suppose it is quite- Obviously it’s… it’s not my intention to sell anything that‘s gonna kill people but yah… I don’t know where they get their alcohol from. (Govan) We ask him about the counterfeit Hennesy. (Leon Strydom) So it’s not really Hennesy. I can’t sell something that’s… what it says, it says flavoring. I’ll have a vodka flavoring, I’ll have a brandy flavoring (Govan) Of the big brands? (Leon Strydom) No, not of the big brands at all. (Govan) Isn’t Hennesy the big brand? (Leon Strydom) It’s just my own stupid label that I’ve put on there (Shamal Ramesar) These products are branded, they have specific formulations that IP belongs to the manufacturer itself, so anybody that is trying to pass it off as a brand is definitely in contravention of the laws. (Govan) We suspect that you are actually supplying a large number of the manufacturers in Johannesburg that make fake alcohol. They get their flavoring from you. (Leon Strydom) I’m just a small housebound business so I buy 5 litres of flavoring from a guy, I put it into smaller bottles, I sell it. It’s not like a multimillion dollar or multi-million- rand business that I’ve got. (Govan) Right now you sell to anyone right? Doesn’t matter if you know what they are doing or not? (Leon Strydom) Well I don’t know what they are doing. (Govan) So you sell to anyone? (Leon Strydom) Yeah. (Govan) In a written response, the police said vetting the authenticity of alcohol isn’t their job but that of SARS. (Govan) That’ll come as little consolation to people like Neo. (Neo Malatji) You need to stop it with this fake alcohol because its killing us. (Shamal Ramesar) We should look at investigating whether these products are causing grievous bodily harm and even look at attempted murder charges.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We take a look at the trade of counterfeit alcohol, how it's made, sold and how it affects you at home.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We have an insider sharing how the fake alcohol is made. Secondly, we confront a brewer where manufacturers of illicit alcohol are purchasing the ingredients. Lastly, we will approach the story from the perspective of the middle class but also explore how it is affecting those of a lower income class, essentially emphasising the point that fake alcohol is a national crisis.
metadata.Summary: Over the last two years, South Africa has seen a spike in counterfeit alcohol making its way to communities across the country. At first it seemed like small scale “backdoor” brewers who were creating cheaper versions of spirits but that’s not the case. We have uncovered a legitimate brewery in Boksburg that supplies ingredients to alcohol manufacturers, who then brew and sell counterfeit alcohol on the black market. They recycle packaging of Remy Martin, Hennesy, Jack Daniels and different variations of gin. The long and short of it is that the boom of fake alcohol is a national crisis that is affected all South Africans, regardless of race or class.
